messages:
alice_cust: Hi team — since yesterday our private deployment started returning KMS errors during inference: 

alice_cust: example errors in logs: 
```
ERROR: KMS unwrap failed: TLS handshake failed (alert handshake failure)
ERROR: failed to fetch key metadata: 403 forbidden
```

alice_cust: This broke model loads intermittently (~10% requests) and causes retries/latency spikes. Any quick ideas?

mike_support: sorry to hear that. are you on Dedicated or Private (VPC) again?

alice_cust: Private (self-hosted control plane in our VPC). Keys are in our HSM cluster that we integrated via the private KMS endpoint.

mike_support: thanks. quick checklist: DNS resolution for the KMS host, outbound SG/NACL allowlist, any egress proxy, and whether the HSM requires client certs (mTLS). can you paste output of these 3 commands from the inference node?
```
dig +short kms.myorg.internal
openssl s_client -connect kms.myorg.internal:443 -servername kms.myorg.internal -brief
curl -v https://kms.myorg.internal/health
```

alice_cust: running now, pasting condensed output: 
```
# dig
10.12.34.5

# openssl (truncated)
CONNECTED(00000003)
140705...: SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed
***
no peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 245 bytes
```

alice_cust: curl gives: "curl: (35) SSL connect error" and some client error 403 intermittently when it does succeed.

sara_infra: that openssl output looks like TLS negotiation failing before cert exchange — could be a TLS MITM from a firewall/proxy or the endpoint dropping connections because of missing SNI or expected client cert. do you use a transparent TLS proxy?

alice_cust: netops says we have an outbound inspection appliance that does TLS interception for some subnets. but our security team explicitly allowlisted the KMS FQDNs — they said they only allow by IP ranges, not by SNI names.

netops_team: quick note: our egress allowlist currently permits 10.12.0.0/20 and we NAT to the internet via a firewall that rewrites SNI for some hosts. we did not explicitly allow the HSM appliance IP range earlier.

mike_support: two likely causes: 1) the inspection appliance is intercepting TLS and not presenting the expected server cert (causes cert verify fail/no peer cert), 2) outbound connections sometimes land on a different backend IP that expects mutual TLS or a different SNI and returns 403. both explain intermittent success.

mike_support: next steps to narrow down: a) traceroute/tcpdump to capture SYN/ACK path, b) curl with verbose TLS info to capture SNI presented, c) request a short tcpdump on the HSM side to see if inbound connection reaches HSM and why it's closed. run these on a failing node:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.12.34.5 and port 443 -w /tmp/kms.pcap & sleep 20; sudo pkill -f tcpdump
sudo strace -f -e trace=network -o /tmp/curl.strace curl -v --resolve kms.myorg.internal:443:10.12.34.5 https://kms.myorg.internal/health
```

alice_cust: got pcap and strace. pcap shows RST from an appliance IP 10.12.1.7 after TLS ClientHello. strace shows no server cert received.

sara_infra: that matches MITM/firewall TLS interception. do you have a policy to bypass interception for HSM traffic? often best practice: egress allowlist by destination IP and set a passthrough rule (no TLS inspect) for the HSM subnet and allow outbound port 443/5696 depending on your HSM. Also ensure the firewall preserves the SNI hostname.

netops_team: we can add a pass-through for 10.12.34.0/24 and whitelist it from inspection. question: does Redwood expect client certs from our side? we didn't configure any client certs.

mike_support: Redwood's private KMS integration has two common modes: 1) TLS server-only where Redwood's control plane will connect using normal TLS (no client cert), using SNI to pick the right tenant; 2) mTLS where customer HSM requires client certificate auth. Your logs show no client cert configured so you are likely in mode 1. if your HSM is actually configured for mTLS, you'd see TLS alert for bad certificate, but your traces indicate no server cert — more like interception.

mike_support: temporary mitigation: route the control-plane egress IPs for KMS to a NAT that bypasses the inspection appliance or add a firewall exception that disables TLS-inspect for the HSM IPs. netops: can you disable TLS inspection for 10.12.34.0/24 and confirm openssl shows the proper server cert chain?

netops_team: applying bypass now.

alice_cust: bypass applied. reran openssl: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = Example Root CA
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = ExampleSubCA, CN = Example SubCA
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = kms.myorg.internal
verify return:1
---
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
```

alice_cust: curl /health now returns 200 consistently. will run inference load tests and report back.

mike_support: great. if load stable, next thing is to ask netops to keep the passthrough rule and add an allowlist for the control-plane IPs so you don't get split routing to different backends. also ensure route table and NAT keep egress source IPs consistent (we use source-based allowlists sometimes).

alice_cust: during one failing trace we also saw 403 from the HSM when connection succeeded. netops pointed out that their proxy rewrites the SNI for some hosts to anonymize telemetry. does Redwood require SNI to match the KMS host?

sara_infra: yes, our control plane relies on SNI to select tenant keys in many private setups. if SNI is rewritten the backend may not find the key (403) or may route to a fallback that expects a different auth. please ensure the proxy preserves SNI for the KMS FQDN.

netops_team: noted. we'll add SNI passthrough/preserve for kms.myorg.internal and add the passthrough rule permanently for the HSM subnet.

mike_support: one more ask — can you share the minimal failing request id from your inference logs (log line with request id) if the issue recurs? we'll correlate with our control-plane logs. also, for future debugging, enable short pcap around the failure and include the ClientHello SNI and TLS alerts.

alice_cust: will do. thanks for triage and clear repro steps. saving this thread for our internal runbook. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Note: created incident 2026-06-03-KMS-EGRESS-123 and assigned to netops_team for permanent firewall config change."
